listCLIContexts.description: First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Flint session control extension. Authenticates the current refresh token without consuming or rotating it. Returns only currently authorized contexts, including an empty list. Listing does not change consent, revoke contexts, or update session state. Read approved scopes from the selected context's token response or /v1/auth-context. No business access is granted. Default order: the order of the contexts approved at the latest consent.

listCreditNoteAllocations.description: Returns every allocation made from a credit note, including reversed ones. Filter by idempotency_key to find the allocation a given request produced. Default order: allocated_at descending, then credit_note_allocation_id descending.

listCreditNotes.description: Returns credit notes for the authenticated merchant, newest first. Filter by invoice_id to see everything credited against one invoice. Default order: created_at descending, then credit_note_id descending.

listCustomDomains.description: Returns domains ordered by created_at descending, then custom_domain_id descending. Default order: created_at descending, then custom_domain_id descending.

listCustomerAddresses.description: Lists the customer's saved addresses with billing and shipping default flags. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_address_id descending.

listCustomerDeletionRequests.description: Lists deletion requests across the selected merchant environment so a merchant can discover and review buyer-created requests. Default order: requested_at descending, then customer_deletion_request_id descending.

listCustomers.description: Returns a paginated list of customers for the authenticated merchant. Without a status filter, returns active and deletion_processing customers; deleted customers appear only when the filter names deleted. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_id descending.

listCustomerTaxExemptions.description: Returns the customer's exemption records ordered by created_at descending, then customer_tax_exemption_id descending. Archived records are excluded by default. Status may filter scheduled, active, expired and archived records, alone or together. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_tax_exemption_id descending.

listCustomerVerifications.description: Lists every status for the required customer_id. Status and supported_actions are computed when read. Flint deletes a verification 8 days after its code and proof expire; customer deletion also removes it. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_verification_id descending.

listDeliveryLocationSets.description: Returns delivery location sets in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_location_set_id ascending.

listDeliveryMethods.description: Returns delivery methods in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_method_id ascending.

listDeliveryProfiles.description: Returns delivery profiles in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_profile_id ascending.

listDeliveryQuotes.description: Returns delivery quotes with status derived identically to individual quote reads. A checkout credential must send its own checkout_session_id and receives the buyer view. Quotes are ordered by created_at and delivery_quote_id ascending. Each page scans at most 500 rows and may contain fewer than page_size items while next_page_token is present. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_quote_id ascending.

listDeliveryRateCallbacks.description: Returns delivery rate callbacks in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_rate_callback_id ascending.

listDeliveryRevocations.description: Returns permanent delivery revocations, newest first by created_at and delivery_revocation_id. Default order: created_at descending, then delivery_revocation_id descending.

listDeliverySelections.description: Returns a checkout session's or an order's delivery selections, current and earlier, newest first by created_at and delivery_selection_id, with economics, lifecycle events, and retention-aware private data. Send checkout_session_id or order_id. A checkout credential must send its own checkout_session_id. With a status filter, each page examines at most 500 selections and may hold fewer than page_size while next_page_token is present. Default order: created_at descending, then delivery_selection_id descending.

listDeliveryZones.description: Returns delivery zones in a stable, cursor-paginated order. Archived resources are excluded by default. Default order: created_at ascending, then delivery_zone_id ascending.

listDevices.description: Returns a paginated list of devices for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then device_id descending.

listDisputes.description: Returns a paginated list of disputes for the authenticated merchant with optional payment, customer, status, reason, case type, action required, and timing filters. Defaults to created_at descending. The amount sort compares amount_money.amount in minor units. The evidence_due_at sort places disputes without deadlines last in either direction. Default order: created_at descending, then dispute_id descending.

listFeedbackReports.description: Lists feedback reports in descending creation order for the credential's merchant and environment. Default order: created_at descending, then feedback_report_id descending.

listFraudWarnings.description: Lists early fraud warnings that card networks reported on your payments, most recently reported first. Filter with `is_actionable=true` to find warnings a full refund can still resolve before a dispute. Default order: reported_at descending, then fraud_warning_id descending.

listFulfillmentEvents.description: Lists provider-neutral fulfillment events. sort_direction applies to both the selected timestamp and the ID tiebreaker. Default order: received_at descending, then fulfillment_event_id descending.

listFulfillmentNotifications.description: Returns persisted fulfillment notification audit records. Results default to newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then fulfillment_notification_id descending.

listFulfillments.description: Returns a paginated list of fulfillments. scheduled_start_at uses the service scheduled start or the start of the pickup, local delivery, or shipment window. For scheduled_start_at and terminal_at, null values sort first ascending and last descending. Default order: created_at descending, then fulfillment_id descending.

listGiftCardFundingDispositions.description: Lists funding dispositions in descending ID order within the authenticated merchant and environment. Filter by idempotency_key to recover a committed command. Default order: gift_card_funding_disposition_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listGiftCardLoads.description: Lists funding lots in descending ID order. Consideration may be null for imported balances whose original purchase price is unknown. The idempotency_key filter recovers a load after a lost command response. Default order: gift_card_load_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listGiftCardNotifications.description: Lists recipient notification identities, schedules and delivery outcomes. No redemption codes or recipient access tokens are returned. Default order: gift_card_notification_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listGiftCardRedemptions.description: Lists reservations and captured redemptions in descending ID order. Retrieve by idempotency_key to recover an operation after a lost response. Default order: gift_card_redemption_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listGiftCards.description: Lists gift cards in descending ID order within the authenticated merchant and environment. Reads include masked codes, posted balance, reserved value and available value. Purchased cards have no expiry or service fees. Default order: gift_card_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listGiftCardTransactions.description: Lists immutable financial entries across the merchant in ascending merchant_sequence order. Per-card sequences and balance snapshots support reconciliation. Reservations and code replacement never create financial debits. Default order: merchant_sequence ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryAdjustments.description: List inventory adjustments. Default order: inventory_adjustment_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryAllocationPolicies.description: List allocation policies. Archived policies are excluded unless you filter by status archived. Default order: inventory_allocation_policy_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryAllocationPolicyRevisions.description: List immutable revisions of an allocation policy, newest first by default. Default order: inventory_allocation_policy_revision_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryCounts.description: List inventory counts. Default order: inventory_count_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryItems.description: List inventory items. Archived items are excluded unless you filter by status archived. Default order: inventory_item_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryLevels.description: List inventory levels. Send expand=inventory_item to render each level's inventory item inline, so a stock table needs no read per row. Filter by inventory_item_status to see only the levels behind items that can be sold. Levels are strongly consistent individually, but pages may reflect different committed instants. Default order: inventory_level_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryMovements.description: List inventory movements, oldest recorded first. Send expand=inventory_item to render each movement's inventory item inline, so a history table needs no read per row. Filter by idempotency_key to recover the movements a command produced. Send sort_direction=desc to read the newest movements first. Default order: created_at ascending, then inventory_movement_id ascending.

listInventoryReceipts.description: List completed inventory receipt effects. Use typed Return filters for reconciliation when the receipt was created by Returns. Default order: inventory_receipt_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryReservations.description: List inventory reservations in ascending inventory_reservation_id order. Omit owner_type to include merchant and order owners. owner_key matches merchant owners only. Default order: inventory_reservation_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInventoryTransfers.description: List inventory transfers. Default order: inventory_transfer_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listInvoiceActivities.description: Returns a read-only history of an invoice for timelines and debugging, newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological order. Read the invoice and the resources each row references for authoritative state. Default order: created_at descending, then invoice_activity_id descending.

listInvoiceDeliveryAttempts.description: Returns email delivery attempts for send and reminder actions. Default order: created_at descending, then invoice_delivery_attempt_id ascending.

listInvoiceManualPayments.description: Lists every manual payment, including reversed payments. Default order: received_at descending, then invoice_manual_payment_id descending.

listInvoicePaymentAttempts.description: Lists card and ACH collection attempts for an invoice in reverse chronological order. Default order: started_at descending, then invoice_payment_attempt_id descending.

listInvoicePaymentTerms.description: Returns a paginated list of invoice payment terms for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then invoice_payment_term_id descending.

listInvoices.description: Returns a paginated list of invoices for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then invoice_id descending.

listLocations.description: List Locations. inventory_allocation_enabled is always included and can be filtered with the Location read scope. The false filter includes Locations without an inventory allocation configuration. Default order: location_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listMeAddresses.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's saved addresses with their billing and shipping default flags. Default order: created_at descending, then customer_address_id descending.

listMeCreditNotes.description: Accepts a customer session, which limits the request to that customer's invoices, or the access token from this invoice's public link, which limits it to this invoice. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the credit notes issued against this invoice, newest first. Default order: issued_at descending, then credit_note_id descending.

listMeDeletionRequests.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. Lists the current buyer's deletion requests in the selected merchant environment, newest first by requested_at. Default order: requested_at descending, then customer_deletion_request_id descending.

listMeFlintWalletCards.description: Returns the current buyer's usable wallet cards in newest-first order. Each flint_wallet_card_id is an opaque per-store handle. store_payment_method_id is null until this store holds a copy. Requires a customer session minted from a live email-code buyer login at a Flint-hosted store account, including a login narrowed to a custom domain. Email links, checkout sessions, grants, merchant-created sessions, and API keys can't see the wallet and get a not-found response. Live and sandbox wallets are isolated. The full card collection is returned in one page. Flint wallet support must be enabled. Default order: most recently added card first.

listMeFulfillmentEvents.description: Lists fulfillment events for an order owned by the current buyer, ordered by occurred_at descending. Internal merchant fields are omitted. order_id is required. Default order: occurred_at descending, then fulfillment_event_id descending.

listMeFulfillments.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists fulfillments for the buyer's orders, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then fulfillment_id descending.

listMeGiftCards.description: Requires a full customer session. Saved access requires possession of a current code or recipient link. Customer associations and purchase history do not authorize access. Replacing a code invalidates saved access; save again with fresh proof. Saved access does not permit spending or reveal a full code. Lists valid saved cards by saved time then card ID, descending. Default order: time the buyer saved the card (descending), then gift_card_id descending.

listMeGiftCardTransactions.description: Requires a full customer session. Saved access requires possession of a current code or recipient link. Customer associations and purchase history do not authorize access. Replacing a code invalidates saved access; save again with fresh proof. Saved access does not permit spending or reveal a full code. Lists the full anonymous balance-change history by per-card sequence, descending. Other holders' identities and order references are omitted. Default order: sequence descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listMeInvoices.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's invoices. Draft invoices are never returned. Default order: created_at descending, then invoice_id descending.

listMeOrderActivities.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource. Default order: created_at descending, then order_activity_id descending.

listMeOrders.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's orders. Default order: created_at descending, then order_id descending.

listMePackages.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists packages in the buyer's shipments, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then package_id descending.

listMePaymentIntents.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's payments. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_intent_id descending.

listMePaymentMethods.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists payment methods in every status except archived, newest first. Filter by status=active for the cards you can charge. Filter by usage off_session to list the payment methods a subscription, automatic invoice, or default payment method can use. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_method_id descending.

listMerchantBillingBalances.description: Returns what the merchant currently owes Flint and owns as account credit by currency. All balances fit on one page, so next_page_token is omitted. Default order: merchant_billing_balance_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listMerchantBillingEntries.description: Returns immutable merchant billing entries for the authenticated merchant environment, newest occurred_at first. Entries in the same second are ordered by type rank, then merchant_billing_entry_id; all three keys are descending. Type ranks are 10 for event_fee, custom_domain, and invoice; 20 for correction; 30 for credit_issued; 40 for credit_applied and credit_refunded; 50 for collection and custom_domain_collection; and 60 for collection_reversal and write_off. An entry can be recorded after entries that occurred later, such as a collection whose bank outcome arrives late. created_at is set when Flint records an entry and never changes or uses a source event timestamp. To pick up new entries, filter on created_after. Overlap successive passes by a few minutes and deduplicate by merchant_billing_entry_id because concurrent commits can become visible after a pass finishes. Re-reading the same entry always returns the same values. To export an interval, use merchant_billing_itemized_v1. It fails with data_unavailable when billing projections or membership history are inconsistent, collection outcome or balance transaction evidence is missing, or an entry is invalid. This list does not run the report interval preflights. Default order: occurred_at descending, then the entry type's rank (descending), then merchant_billing_entry_id descending.

listMerchantBillingInvoices.description: Returns invoices issued by Flint for the authenticated merchant environment. Default order: merchant_billing_invoice_id descending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listMerchantPartnerAppInstalls.description: Lists partner app installs on the authenticated merchant, across live and test mode. Requires a live API key. Default order: partner_app_install_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listMerchantSignups.description: Lists the signups of your partner apps, newest first, then by `merchant_signup_id`. A merchant that owns no app gets an empty list. Live only: test credentials get 403 FORBIDDEN with reason live_mode_required, and a key linked to a partner app install gets 403 FORBIDDEN with reason linked_key_not_allowed. Partner app tokens can't call it. Default order: created_at descending, then merchant_signup_id descending.

listMeRefunds.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's refunds. Default order: created_at descending, then refund_id descending.

listMeReturns.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's Returns. Filter by order, return number, reason, status, decision, merchandise, resolution, or creation and update time. Default order: created_at descending, then return_id descending.

listMeShipments.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists shipments for the buyer's orders and Returns, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then shipment_id descending.

listMeSubscriptionPaymentRetries.description: Returns a subscription's manual payment retries, newest first. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_payment_retry_id descending.

listMeSubscriptions.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's subscriptions. Subscriptions without a next_billing_at never match next_billing_after or next_billing_before, and sort last with sort_by=next_billing_at in either direction. subscription_plan is always included without expand: the plan's current summary, or null when the subscription has no plan. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_id descending.

listMeTickets.description: Lists the event tickets on the buyer's orders, newest first, with each ticket's admission code for showing its QR code. Voided tickets are listed without an admission code. Admission codes go only to buyers Flint verified: a buyer session whose email Flint confirmed (hosted sign-in or the paid checkout's sign-in), on orders whose buyer_email is that email, or an order link from the paying checkout or emailed to the order's buyer_email. Merchant access links, customer sessions created with an API key, and checkout links a merchant reads or requests after payment list the tickets without admission codes; use rotate-code to deliver tickets yourself. Default order: created_at descending, then ticket_id descending.

listModifierGroups.description: List modifier groups. Default order: created_at descending, then modifier_group_id descending.

listModifierSets.description: List modifier sets. Default order: created_at descending, then modifier_set_id descending.

listOrderActivities.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource. Default order: created_at descending, then order_activity_id descending.

listOrderCharges.description: Returns the order's charges sorted by ID in ascending order. Default order: order_charge_id ascending.

listOrderEdits.description: Lists immutable edits for this order, newest created_at first, with descending order_edit_id as the tiebreaker. Defaults to 20 results. Keep filters unchanged when using a page token. Default order: created_at descending, then order_edit_id descending.

listOrderLineItems.description: Returns the order's line items sorted by ID in ascending order. Default order: order_line_item_id ascending.

listOrderPaymentAttempts.description: Returns payment attempts for the order, newest first. Checkout-session callers see only attempts created by their own session. A list filtered by idempotency_key omits pending_actions; read the attempt by ID to get them. Default order: started_at descending, then order_payment_attempt_id descending.

listOrders.description: Returns a paginated list of orders for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then order_id descending.

listPackageItems.description: Lists order line quantities contained in packages. Default order: created_at descending, then package_item_id descending.

listPackages.description: Lists package records, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then package_id descending.

listPartnerAppCredentials.description: Lists active and removed credentials, ordered by partner_app_credential_id ascending. Default order: partner_app_credential_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listPartnerAppInstalls.description: Returns installs for a partner app owned by the authenticated merchant. Each active grant that can read the merchant profile carries `merchant_readiness`: whether the installed merchant can take payments and receive payouts in that environment, and how many requirements are due. Use it to find merchants who still need to finish onboarding without exchanging each install’s token. A live partner app token can list its own app's installs, with the same filters and summaries as the owner; a merchant-bound token lists at most its merchant's install. Default order: partner_app_install_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listPartnerApps.description: Returns partner apps owned by the authenticated merchant. Default order: partner_app_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listPaymentIntentActivities.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history for a payment intent. Read the payment intent or referenced resource for authoritative state; this log does not replace webhooks or a ledger. Use sort_direction=asc for a chronological timeline. Page tokens are bound to the payment intent, merchant, environment, activity_type filter, and sort direction. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_intent_activity_id descending.

listPaymentIntents.description: Returns a paginated list of payment intents for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_intent_id descending.

listPaymentLinks.description: Returns a paginated list of payment links for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_link_id descending.

listPaymentMethodDomains.description: Returns payment method domains ordered by payment_method_domain_id ascending in the selected Flint environment. Page tokens are opaque, bind to the list parameters, and return a validation error when invalid or mismatched. Default order: payment_method_domain_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listPaymentMethods.description: Lists payment methods in every status except archived, newest first. Filter by status=active for the cards you can charge. Optionally filter to a customer. Filter by usage off_session to list the payment methods a subscription, automatic invoice, or default payment method can use. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_method_id descending.

listPaymentReviews.description: Lists payment reviews, most recently opened first. A review opens when a `review` rule matches a payment the bank approved. Every status is included unless you filter by `status`. Default order: opened_at descending, then payment_review_id descending.

listPaymentSplits.description: Lists splits where you are either party, newest first, then by payment_split_id descending. Read splits you collected or received, with your own credentials and money_movement.payment_splits.read. Install tokens can't read splits. Test splits are in the collecting merchant's sandbox and the seller's test grant's sandbox. Consumers include marketplace payment pages and seller reconciliation. Default order: created_at descending, then payment_split_id descending.

listPayoutDestinations.description: Returns a paginated list of payout destinations available to the authenticated merchant. The account owner adds a destination in the `payouts` embedded component, opened with POST /v1/merchant-account-sessions; Flint never takes bank details through the API. Default order: created_at descending, then payout_destination_id descending.

listPayouts.description: Returns a paginated list of payouts with optional filters for status, currency, destination, method, and timing. Default order: created_at descending, then payout_id descending.

listPlatformFeeBalances.description: Lists your partner apps' platform fee balances, one per partner app and currency, newest first. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: time Flint opened the balance (descending), then platform_fee_balance_id descending.

listPlatformFeeBalanceTransactions.description: Lists your partner apps' platform fee ledger, newest occurred_at first, then by platform_fee_balance_transaction_id. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: occurred_at descending, then platform_fee_balance_transaction_id descending.

listPlatformFeePayouts.description: Lists payouts from your partner apps' fee balances to your merchant balance, newest first, then by platform_fee_payout_id. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: created_at descending, then platform_fee_payout_id descending.

listPlatformFees.description: Lists the platform fees your partner apps charged, newest first, then by platform_fee_id. Reads the merchant that owns the partner app, with its own credentials and money_movement.platform_fees.read; partner app tokens can't. Live records are in your live environment. Test records are in your default sandbox at the time the payment was created. A merchant that owns no partner app gets an empty list. Default order: created_at descending, then platform_fee_id descending.

listPriceListPrices.description: Lists the variant prices in a price list. Filter by variant_id or product_id. Results default to created_at descending, with price_list_price_id descending as the tiebreak. Default order: created_at descending, then price_list_price_id descending.

listPriceLists.description: Lists price lists. Archived lists are excluded unless the status filter explicitly names archived. Results default to created_at descending, with price_list_id descending as the tiebreak. Default order: created_at descending, then price_list_id descending.

listProductOptions.description: List product options. Default order: position ascending, then option_id ascending.

listProducts.description: Returns a paginated list of products for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then product_id descending.

listProductVariants.description: List product variants. Default order: position ascending, then variant_id ascending.

listPromotionCodes.description: Returns a paginated list of promotion codes in every status, ordered by created_at descending, then promotion_code_id descending. Archived codes are excluded unless status=archived. Default order: created_at descending, then promotion_code_id descending.

listPromotions.description: Returns a paginated list of promotions for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then promotion_id descending.

listReaders.description: Lists readers newest first, then by `reader_id`. Archived readers are listed only when the `status` filter names `archived`. Default order: created_at descending, then reader_id descending.

listRefunds.description: Returns a paginated list of refunds for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then refund_id descending.

listReports.description: Lists reports using opaque pagination. Default order: created_at descending, then report_id descending.

listReturnActivities.description: Read the merchant history of a Return for timelines and audit. Read the referenced resources for current state. listReturnDispositions.description: List merchandise dispositions. Omitting return_id lists dispositions across every Return for the merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then return_disposition_id descending.

listReturnInspections.description: List inspection observations. Omitting return_id lists inspections across every Return for the merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then return_inspection_id descending.

listReturnLineItems.description: List the line items on a Return with their quantity counters, eligibility, frozen display identity, and return value. Default order: created_at descending, then return_line_item_id descending.

listReturnPolicies.description: List Return policies with their status. Include the current revision with expand=current_revision. Default order: created_at descending, then return_policy_id descending.

listReturnPolicyRevisions.description: List every published revision of a Return policy. Default order: created_at descending, then return_policy_revision_id descending.

listReturnReasons.description: List Return reasons, including Flint-provided defaults and merchant-defined reasons. Flint reasons have a created_at of 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, so they follow your own. Default order: created_at descending, then return_reason_id descending.

listReturnReceipts.description: List merchandise receipts. Omitting return_id lists receipts across every Return for the merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then return_receipt_id descending.

listReturnResolutions.description: List resolutions. Filter by corrects_return_resolution_id to retrieve the correction history for a resolution that already settled. Default order: created_at descending, then return_resolution_id descending.

listReturns.description: List Returns for the merchant, filtered by order, customer, status, decision, merchandise, resolution, or creation window. listRiskListItems.description: Lists a list's values, newest first. Default order: created_at descending, then risk_list_item_id descending.

listRiskLists.description: Lists risk lists, newest first, including Flint's default block lists. Archived lists appear only when status includes archived. Default order: created_at descending, then risk_list_id descending.

listRiskRules.description: Lists risk rules, newest first, including Flint's default rules. By default, includes active and inactive rules. Archived rules appear only when status includes archived. listShipments.description: Lists shipment execution records, newest created first. Default order: created_at descending, then shipment_id descending.

listSubscriptionDeliveryMigrationFailure.description: Each subscription is previewed before its delivery method changes. Progress and per-subscription failures remain available after completion. Default order: subscription_id ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listSubscriptionDeliveryMigrations.description: Each subscription is previewed before its delivery method changes. Progress and per-subscription failures remain available after completion. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_delivery_migration_id descending.

listSubscriptionOffers.description: List subscription offers. Offer changes affect new signups only. Existing subscriptions keep their terms. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_offer_id descending.

listSubscriptionPaymentRetries.description: Returns a subscription's manual payment retries, newest first. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_payment_retry_id descending.

listSubscriptionPlans.description: Returns a paginated list of subscription plans for the authenticated merchant. Default order: created_at descending, then subscription_plan_id descending.

listSubscriptions.description: Returns a paginated list of subscriptions for the authenticated merchant. listTaxCalculationCallbacks.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Default order: created_at descending, then tax_calculation_callback_id descending.

listWebhookDeliveryAttempts.description: Returns the attempts recorded for a specific webhook delivery. Global partner-source records are invisible in sandbox mode; a direct reference returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. Default order: attempt_number ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listWebhookEndpoints.description: Returns a page of webhook endpoints for the authenticated merchant. Sandbox reads omit global partner-source records. Filters selecting only partner_app or installed_merchants return an empty collection. Direct resource reads of partner-source records return 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND in sandbox mode; exact-ID list filters return an empty collection when no visible records match. Default order: created_at descending, then webhook_endpoint_id descending.

listWebhookEvents.description: Returns recent canonical webhook events for the authenticated merchant. Sandbox reads omit global partner-source records. Filters selecting only partner_app or installed_merchants return an empty collection. Direct resource reads of partner-source records return 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND in sandbox mode; exact-ID list filters return an empty collection when no visible records match. Default order: created_at descending, then webhook_event_id descending.

listWebhookEventTypes.description: Returns every webhook event type you can use in enabled_events and event filters, with the event sources each type is valid for. Default order: event_type ascending; this key uniquely orders the results.

listWorkloadIdentities.description: Returns identities in the authenticated environment, ordered by created_at descending and workload_identity_id descending by default. Archived identities are excluded unless status includes archived. Default order: created_at descending, then workload_identity_id descending.

lookupEmailPreferenceLink.description: Reads an emailed preference token without signing the buyer in. The merchant key must match the token's merchant and environment. Tokens belong in the request body and must stay on your backend.

lookupEmailPreferences.description: Reads an address's email preferences without putting it in a URL. Matches after trimming surrounding whitespace and ignoring case. Returns the same shape as the customer preference read. For an address without a current customer, customer_id and version are null. With multiple matching customers, returns the first customer in ID order. A category with no stored choice is enabled. Merchants cannot change these preferences.

lookupGiftCard.description: Evaluates a full bearer code in a request body. Codes contain 16 ASCII Crockford base32 characters, accept lowercase and hyphens, and normalize O to 0 and I/L to 1. Lookup is side-effect-free and never reserves funds. Unknown, other-merchant and unusable codes return the same error.

lookupTicket.description: Looks up an admission code in the authenticated merchant and environment, including voided tickets. ASCII lowercase, spaces and hyphens are accepted; O maps to 0 and I/L to 1. Malformed codes return 400 INVALID_VALUE; an unknown or foreign code returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND at admission_code. The code is never returned.

Other actions reject tracking fields. mark_shipped, mark_in_transit, and mark_out_for_delivery optionally set expected_delivery_at; send null to clear it. Delivery preserves the estimate as history. expected_version is optional and rejects a stale resource version when supplied. pauseMeSubscription.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Pauses a subscription immediately. pause_duration_cycles counts delivery intervals on prepaid subscriptions and billing intervals otherwise; omit it for an indefinite pause. A pause with a duration resumes automatically at scheduled_resume_at. Repeating the stored pause length returns the paused subscription; a different length returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason field_locked and param pause_duration_cycles and requires resuming first. A buyer's pause follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change. A closed store is read-only: commerce changes fail with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status. Receipts and order history remain readable.

pauseSubscription.description: Pauses a subscription immediately. pause_duration_cycles counts delivery intervals on prepaid subscriptions and billing intervals otherwise; omit it for an indefinite pause. payOrder.description: Starts or resumes a payment attempt on the order. Starting a subscription requires buyer_contact.email or an email already saved on the checkout session or order. Set action to pay to charge the full outstanding balance, confirm_payment_intents to confirm order-owned payment intents, setup to save a newly collected token on a zero-balance order, or resume to continue an attempt after a pending client action. Each action accepts only its own fields. Only confirm_payment_intents accepts completion_behavior. A pay action without payment_source is valid only when the outstanding balance is zero. To continue a resumable attempt, send action: resume with order_payment_attempt_id and a new Idempotency-Key. A Tap to Pay reader returns requires_action, is_resumable true, and a card_presentment pending action with stripe.terminal_payment_intent authority for the Stripe Terminal SDK. After the app collects and confirms, resume reads the outcome: authorization or capture applies it, processing keeps the attempt processing, and no card or a decline keeps it requires_action with the same authority. A decline updates last_payment_error without ending the attempt; cancel to give up. An exact retry of the original request with its Idempotency-Key returns the stored response if the request completed, or recovers the same attempt if it was interrupted. Payment intents with manual capture return an active authorization instead of settling immediately. A replay preserves the original HTTP status and domain result. Replays return no URL token or Stripe client secret; pending_actions is empty when action authority was stripped. Read the attempt to recover its current permitted actions. Read GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/payment-attempts/{order_payment_attempt_id} for the attempt's current state.

previewPartnerInstallAuthorization.description: Validates the install link inputs and returns the partner app metadata and requested permissions for the consent screen. This route takes no credential, and Flint ignores a single Authorization header, as GET /v1/oauth/authorize does. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization. Flint ignores unrecognized parameters.

processReturn.description: Record decisions, receipts, inspections, dispositions, and resolutions for an existing requested or open Return in one request. On a requested Return, send one decision for every requested line; missing decisions fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `status_not_reached`. Omit completion_mode to use the shared pinned policy mode, or automatic when none sets a mode; disagreeing policies require an explicit completion_mode. On an open Return, omit decision and completion_mode to keep committed values, or send those values unchanged; changed values fail with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `field_locked`. completion_blockers includes resolution_not_selected for any uncovered approved quantity alongside blockers for unfinished resolutions. A line can be processed here only while it has no receipt, inspection, disposition, or resolution; otherwise ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED has reason unsupported_state and param line_items[i].return_line_item_id. A receipt location that differs from a line's committed location fails with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED, reason field_locked, and param receipt.receiving_location_id. Missing receipt or receipt.receiving_location_id fails with INVALID_REQUEST and detail REQUIRED. For each line, received_quantity must equal its committed return_required_quantity. Send inspection exactly when the line requires inspection, with acceptance_status accepted. Refunds, payments, replacement orders, and inventory updates complete asynchronously. expected_version is optional and checked only when sent. If the Return has changed since that version, the request fails with VERSION_CONFLICT. When an automatic refund can no longer run through the original payment's provider, the request fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; on a decision, send automatic_resolution_type as null to resolve manually; on a resolution, choose another resolution_type, such as no_monetary_action, and reimburse the buyer another way. Requires an idempotency key and all three scopes: commerce.returns.write, commerce.returns.operations.write, and commerce.returns.resolutions.write.

reauthorizeCLIDevice.description: First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Flint session control extension. Starts device consent bound to the current session and user without consuming the refresh token. Without scope_mode, approval replaces consent; denial or expiry leaves consent unchanged. Redeem using the device_code grant to rotate the latest family token. Set scope_mode=additive and context_id to request additional space-separated scope names for one existing context. Merchant and environment are derived from that context; conflicting hints return invalid_context. Approval unions only browser-approved additions with that context's existing scopes and preserves all other contexts. No implicit bootstrap scopes are added. Unsupported or environment-disallowed scopes return HTTP 400 invalid_scope; browser denial returns access_denied when polling. Partial approval succeeds and scope in the token response is authoritative. A superseded consent review returns expired_token when its device code is redeemed; start a new review. The existing session remains active.

receiveInventoryTransfer.description: Adds in-transit stock to the destination location. Optional condition targets split the received quantity by condition. Call it only when receive is in supported_actions. Lines carry cumulative targets, not deltas. Returns a result with inventory_transfer as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the inventory transfer by ID.

refreshCustomerSession.description: Rotates a customer session secret and refresh token without a merchant API key. Reusing a rotated refresh token revokes the session family. Use one fixed idempotency key per session: Flint scopes the key to the refresh token, so concurrent refreshes replay the same pair. On `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS`, retry with the same key and token.

refreshMerchantAccountSession.description: Creates a fresh provider session from a signed launch token after rechecking the authenticated principal, merchant environment, account controller, and component grant. An onboarding session can refresh only sandbox launch tokens created by the same user with an onboarding session. The sandbox is pinned by the launch token, which is the merchant's default sandbox for an onboarding session. Live onboarding requires a live API key or live CLI login. A partner install token works in live mode only while its app's merchant_onboarding platform capability is active; otherwise it gets 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with the reason its platform status gives: platform_onboarding_required, platform_pending_review, platform_rejected, or platform_capability_inactive. Refresh requires the same credential that created the launch token. For an install token, that is any access token for the same environment grant and consent; revoking the install or grant, or authorizing again, ends the launch token. A same-key, same-input retry replays the encrypted original result for 24 hours, including its original credentials and expiries. Replay may return an expired credential. Use a new key for a new launch or refresh.

regenerateInvoicePublicLink.description: Revokes the current buyer-access link and all checkout credentials derived from it, then returns a new public_url. The current checkout session and its payment lineage are preserved. Fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` and reason `in_progress` when the invoice's customer is being deleted or has been deleted. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key.

releaseDeliverySelection.description: Clears the checkout's provisional selection: releases its stock hold, removes its delivery charges, and recalculates the order. Available while supported_actions lists release. A checkout credential can release only its own session's selection; any other is refused as not found.

releaseFulfillmentHold.description: Releases a merchant hold and restores the previous fulfillment status. An active payment hold must lift first. Schedules and progress timestamps are preserved and no buyer notification is sent. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

releaseInventoryReservation.description: Releases held or committed quantity back to available stock, for example when the buyer leaves or you cancel after payment. Call it only when release is in supported_actions. Lines carry cumulative targets: resending targets already applied succeeds even after the reservation closes. Returns a result with inventory_reservation as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the inventory reservation by ID.

releaseReturnResolution.description: Release a confirmed resolution that is waiting on a manual release. Available only while action_reason is manual_release.

removeMeGiftCard.description: Requires a full customer session. Saved access requires possession of a current code or recipient link. Customer associations and purchase history do not authorize access. Replacing a code invalidates saved access; save again with fresh proof. Saved access does not permit spending or reveal a full code. Removes only this buyer's saved access without changing funds or other holders' access. A repeated removal without an idempotency key fails with `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` because saved access is already absent. Reusing the same idempotency key replays the original removal snapshot without restoring saved access. Idempotency keys are scoped to the buyer, merchant, environment, and operation. A replay cannot restore removed or revoked saved access. A closed store is read-only: commerce changes fail with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status. Receipts and order history remain readable.

removeOrderDiscounts.description: Removes pending applied discounts or deferred promotions from an order. Send at least one ID across order_discount_ids and deferred_promotion_ids. Deferred promotions can be removed before payment. Redeemed or canceled discounts are settlement history and cannot be removed.

removeOrderGiftCard.description: Removes a selected gift card without moving value. The expected_version must still match the order version. Selections cannot change during an active payment attempt. Retry a lost response with the same idempotency key to recover the original selection result.

removeSubscriptionPromotions.description: Removes 1 to 5 unique active or scheduled promotions from a subscription. Future renewal orders omit them; paid orders and the unpaid past_due order keep their discounts. Removal keeps consumed cycles for reattachment and does not return a promotion use. Offer promotions cannot be removed. Requires commerce.subscriptions.write.

renewMeSubscription.description: Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires a full buyer session and an idempotency key. Send expected_version to reject concurrent changes. Retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt, including when the payment is declined. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment. When the store cannot accept payments, a new payment fails with 409 MERCHANT_NOT_READY and reason processing_restricted. Changes billed at a future renewal remain available. A closed store is read-only: commerce changes fail with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status. Receipts and order history remain readable.

renewSubscription.description: Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires an idempotency key; retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt, including when the payment is declined. Inspect order_payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment.

reopenReturn.description: Reopen a completed Return to record late compensating facts. Reopening sets completion_mode to manual, so complete the Return again with /complete once completion_blockers is empty. Confirmed money movements are never edited backward, so a monetary fix is a new correction resolution.

reportInventoryTransferLoss.description: Records in-transit stock as lost. Call it only when report_loss is in supported_actions. Lines carry cumulative targets, not deltas. Returns a result with inventory_transfer as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the inventory transfer by ID.

repriceOrderDiscounts.description: Recalculates pending discounts and automatic promotions for a mutable order. The request body is optional. Send expected_version to reject a mutation based on an outdated order read.

resendMerchantSignupCode.description: Emails the owner a new code for a `pending` signup. The new code replaces the old one and resets the attempt count; a code email still queued for the old code is never sent. A signup sends at most 3 codes (409 LIMIT_REACHED with reason verification_codes and limit 3), within the per-mailbox send caps of create. The app's create_merchants capability is checked again, so a paused platform sends no more codes. Any other status returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason unsupported_state. It is a message operation, not a lifecycle action, so supported_actions never lists it. Live only: test credentials get 403 FORBIDDEN with reason live_mode_required, and a key linked to a partner app install gets 403 FORBIDDEN with reason linked_key_not_allowed. Partner app tokens can't call it.

resendWebhookDelivery.description: Sends the event to the delivery's endpoint now, including while automatic retries are pending. A failed resend doesn't change the automatic schedule. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

resetDemoSession.description: Ends the active or provisioning demo session identified by demo_session_id for this client and provisions a fresh one. A client that lost its create response gets the current session ID from current_resource.resource_id on ALREADY_EXISTS. A retry with the same idempotency key and body replays the replacement before checking the current session, including its secret during the secret delivery window. After that window, the retry returns ALREADY_EXISTS with the current session reference. The daily cap applies only to fresh executions. Omit template to use quickstart; an explicit empty or unsupported value is invalid.

resetSandbox.description: Deletes a sandbox's data and keeps its identity and connections. The default sandbox can be reset too. A test credential (API key, CLI login, or workload token) with `developer.sandboxes.write` can reset only the sandbox it is bound to; any other `sandbox_id` gets 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, and the credential keeps working after the reset. The sandbox keeps its `sandbox_id`, name, and `is_default`; every credential bound to it, including API keys, workload identities, CLI logins, and connected app installs; its webhook endpoints with their secrets and API versions; its test payment account and readiness; its payment method, checkout, and custom domains; and its processing fee assignments. Everything else is deleted: catalog, customers, orders, payments, invoices, subscriptions, test clocks, settings, locations, risk lists, request logs, events, deliveries, and idempotency keys. Returns the same sandbox with `status` `active` and a new `updated_at`. Requests that start while the reset runs get 409 `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS` with reason `sandbox_resetting`; retry them after Retry-After. A second reset while one is running gets 409 `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`. Failed resets retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 60 minutes, with at most eight attempts. Each attempt counts when it starts, including interrupted attempts. `reset_failed_at` records when a reset stops. If deletion has not started, the sandbox keeps its previous data and accepts requests again. If deletion has started, requests get 409 `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` with reason `sandbox_reset_failed`, without Retry-After. Reset it again to resume, or archive a non-default sandbox. A successful reset clears `reset_failed_at`. Requests already running when the reset started finish against the old data, and their results don't survive the reset. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the recorded response; a new key resets again. Each sandbox allows one reset every 10 seconds and 500 resets per UTC day, shared by every credential that can reset it; past either limit the request gets 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with Retry-After, and a same-key retry doesn't count again. See the [sandboxes guide](/docs/guides/sandboxes#reset-a-sandbox).

resolveCustomerDeletionRequest.description: Approves or rejects a pending deletion request. Approval returns processing while account data and buyer credentials are deleted asynchronously. A failed deletion can be approved again but cannot be rejected. Approval is blocked while the customer has non-canceled subscriptions or usable saved payment methods.

resolveOrderInventoryException.description: Marks a paid inventory failure as resolved after an operator has completed manual inventory remediation.

resolvePaymentLink.description: Creates a buyer checkout session from an active payment link. Catalog-backed modifier availability is frozen onto the checkout session and selected modifiers are resolved onto the backing order. For a retry after an uncertain response, reuse the original idempotency key and resolution_context.

resumeMeSubscription.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Asks Flint to resume a paused subscription. The request is accepted while the subscription is still paused, with `resume_requested_at` set. Flint then makes it active, or past_due while an overdue period is collected, and sends subscription.resumed. While prepaid deliveries remain, resuming makes no charge and shifts later deliveries and the next charge by the length of the pause. If Flint can't resume it, it stays paused, resume_requested_at clears, and Flint sends subscription.updated. Any other status fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`. To undo a scheduled cancellation, PATCH the subscription with cancel_at_period_end set to false. When the store cannot accept payments, a new payment fails with 409 MERCHANT_NOT_READY and reason processing_restricted. Changes billed at a future renewal remain available. A closed store is read-only: commerce changes fail with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status. Receipts and order history remain readable.

resumeSubscription.description: Asks Flint to resume a paused subscription. The request is accepted while the subscription is still paused, with `resume_requested_at` set. Flint then makes it active, or past_due while an overdue period is collected, and sends subscription.resumed. While prepaid deliveries remain, resuming makes no charge and shifts later deliveries and the next charge by the length of the pause. If Flint can't resume it, it stays paused, resume_requested_at clears, and Flint sends subscription.updated. Any other status fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`. To undo a scheduled cancellation, PATCH the subscription with cancel_at_period_end set to false.

retryOrderEditRefund.description: Refunds the edit's remaining frozen money after refund processing has failed. Pending and succeeded linked refunds count toward the edit's refunded value. Omit the body or destinations to reuse the edit's original destinations. Retry is unavailable while a linked refund is pending, when nothing remains, or when a payment is disputed. While Flint is still processing the original refund and no linked refund exists, supported_actions is empty and retry returns in_progress. If processing ends without creating a refund, retry becomes available. Use a new Idempotency-Key for a new retry attempt, and the same key and body to recover its lost response. The response contains only refunds created by this attempt.

retryReturnDisposition.description: Retry a failed disposition with the same immutable intent. Disposition and effect identities are preserved, so a retry does not move stock twice.

retryReturnResolution.description: Retry a failed resolution. For gift_card_refund_destination_required, send gift_card_refund_destination: new_gift_card to persist the destination before starting the new attempt. The override is accepted for refund, exchange, and corrections of resolutions other than store_credit. A new attempt starts, historical payment and refund IDs stay on the resolution, and a late event from an earlier attempt cannot settle the new attempt. Fails with ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED, with the line's current_status, when a Return line the resolution covers is no longer approved, such as after it was canceled, and with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when an approved line no longer has the quantity the resolution covers. Retry is available only when failure_code allows it, and supported_actions includes retry in that case. A failure that retry cannot fix fails with `ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`; cancel the resolution instead.

returnInventoryTransferToOrigin.description: Puts in-transit stock back at the origin location. Call it only when return_to_origin is in supported_actions. Lines carry cumulative targets, not deltas. Returns a result with inventory_transfer as its primary resource and inventory_levels for the levels changed. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the inventory transfer by ID.

reverseCreditNoteAllocation.description: Reverses an allocation and reopens that much of the invoice balance. The original allocation keeps its row and gains reversed_at, so the history stays append-only. Reversing the allocation that closed an invoice moves it from credited back to open or partially_paid. Reversing credit on a paid invoice that also has collected payments moves it to partially_paid.

reverseInvoiceManualPayment.description: Reverses the named manual payment in full and returns its amount to the invoice balance. To correct an amount, reverse the payment and record the correct payment. A retry with the same idempotency key replays the result; a retry without a key fails once the payment is already reversed.

revokeAPIKey.description: Permanently revokes an external API key and returns metadata with status revoked.

revokeCustomerSession.description: Revokes one customer session in the selected merchant environment. This does not revoke an independent Flint Account buyer session.

revokeCustomerSessions.description: Revokes every customer session for one customer in the selected merchant environment. Flint Account buyer sessions remain independent.

revokeMerchantPartnerAppInstall.description: Disconnects a partner app from the authenticated merchant: revokes the install, its environment grants, its refresh tokens and linked API keys, and deletes linked webhook endpoints. The app is sent partner_app_install.revoked with revoked_by: merchant. A new request against an already revoked install returns empty ended-access arrays. Unlinked API keys and webhook endpoints keep working. To reconnect, install the app again.

revokeMeSession.description: Signs out the current customer session using its current server-held secret, including after expiry, after revocation, or after its parent buyer session or grant ended. Repeating the call preserves revoked_at. A secret rotated away by refresh is invalid. Flint Account buyer sessions remain independent.

revokeOAuthToken.description:
RFC 7009 token revocation for partner apps and flint-cli. Partner apps authenticate with client assertions, HTTP Basic, or client_secret. Assertion rules match the token endpoint. Self-signed private_key_jwt assertions (iss=sub=client_id; ES256, ES384, PS256, RS256, or EdDSA; a single-use jti; exp at most five minutes ahead) are verified against public_key or jwks_url credentials, so sign a fresh one with a new jti for each request. Workload identity assertions have the external issuer as iss and are verified with that issuer's published keys; they use RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, or ES512, expire no more than one hour and 60 seconds ahead, and need no jti. Revoking a partner app token ends that token only; token_type_hint is only a hint. Unknown, expired, and other clients' tokens return 200 with no change. Revoking a token never changes an install or grant.

For flint-cli, revoking an access or refresh token ends its CLI session and invalidates the session's tokens. The public client sends client_id=flint-cli without a secret or Authorization header. Send application/x-www-form-urlencoded; success has an empty body. Repeated Authorization fields return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a NOT_ALLOWED detail at Authorization in the Flint error envelope.

revokePartnerAppEnvironmentGrant.description: The installing merchant, the partner app owner, or a live partner app token for the app can revoke a single test or live environment grant for an install. A live token can revoke a test grant. A merchant-bound token can revoke only its merchant's grants; other installs return 404. This revokes linked API keys and deletes linked webhook endpoints in that environment. Revoking the last grant also revokes the install and ends its remaining links. Unlinked keys and endpoints keep working.

revokePartnerAppInstall.description: The installing merchant, the partner app owner, or a live partner app token for the app can revoke an install and all of its environment grants. A merchant-bound token can revoke only its merchant's install; other installs return 404. The owner and the app's tokens record revoked_by partner_app, and a token records no revoked_by_user_id. This also revokes linked API keys and deletes linked webhook endpoints. Unlinked keys and endpoints keep working. Reinstalling does not restore ended access.

rotateDeliveryRateCallbackSecret.description: Replaces the callback's shared secret and returns the callback with the new secret and its delivery_rate_callback_signing_key_id once. Flint signs with both keys for one hour. A callback without hmac returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason secret_not_issued; PATCH signing_methods to include hmac to issue the first secret.

rotateGiftCardCode.description: Invalidates the old bearer credential and generates a new code for the same gift card. Balances, funding, reservations and refund history are preserved. Requires commerce.gift_cards.secrets.write. Include notification to send the new private recipient link. Retired links cannot open the current code. The new full code is available in this response and authorized retries only within 24 hours, while that code remains current. expected_version fences the gift card version.

rotateMerchantSignupAuthorizationCodes.description: Mints new authorization codes for a completed signup's grants that were never exchanged, bound to the signup's code_challenge, and supersedes the earlier ones. Use it when the verify response was lost or the codes expired before you exchanged them. It works only within 24 hours of completed_at and while nothing else has happened to the install: any revoke, or an authorization of the app on the consent screen, ends it for good. Refused with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED: reason already_applied once every grant has been exchanged (mint partner app tokens with grant_type=client_credentials instead), unsupported_state when the signup isn't completed, and not_offered once the window or the install's state ends rotation; the owner then reauthorizes on the consent screen. An idempotent replay returns the signup without the codes. It is a code rotation, not a lifecycle action, so supported_actions never lists it. Live only: test credentials get 403 FORBIDDEN with reason live_mode_required, and a key linked to a partner app install gets 403 FORBIDDEN with reason linked_key_not_allowed. Partner app tokens can't call it.

rotatePartnerAppSecret.description: Rotates an existing client secret, returned once. An app without a secret returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason secret_not_issued. Issue its first secret with PATCH /v1/partner-apps/{partner_app_id} and client_secret_enabled: true. The previous secret keeps working until previous_secret_expires_at: 24 hours by default, or the time in expire_previous_secret_at, up to 7 days. Send a time at or before now to stop the previous secret immediately, for example when it leaked. Rotating again during an overlap ends the older secret at once.

rotateTaxCalculationCallbackSecret.description: Tax calculation callback configuration is scoped to the selected environment. Partner installation tokens are unsupported. Issues an HMAC secret and adds hmac when needed. Returns the new secret once. The previous secret remains valid during the same overlap as delivery callbacks.

rotateTicketCode.description: Replaces the ticket's admission code and returns the new code once, in admission_code. The old code stops working immediately. Use it to deliver tickets yourself with send_ticket_emails turned off. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key within 24 hours returns the code again while the ticket is unchanged since this rotation; after any later change, including another rotation, it returns the ticket without admission_code. A voided ticket returns 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason unsupported_state.

rotateWebhookEndpointSecret.description: Rotates an existing shared secret. An endpoint without hmac returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason secret_not_issued; PATCH signing_methods to include hmac to issue the first secret. The secret is returned once. The replaced secret keeps signing deliveries until previous_secret_expires_at: 24 hours by default, or expire_previous_secret_at, up to 7 days. Send a time at or before now to stop the replaced secret immediately, for example when it leaked. Rotating again during an overlap ends the older secret at once. Partner-source endpoints are global configuration. Changes to them or their events and deliveries require a live-mode credential or a Dashboard session, including test events and endpoints subscribed only to test installed-merchant events. Test credentials fail with `FORBIDDEN` and reason `live_mode_required`, including on idempotent replay.

saveMeGiftCard.description: Requires a full customer session. Saved access requires possession of a current code or recipient link. Customer associations and purchase history do not authorize access. Replacing a code invalidates saved access; save again with fresh proof. Saved access does not permit spending or reveal a full code. Idempotency keys are scoped to the buyer, merchant, environment, and operation. A replay cannot restore removed or revoked saved access. A closed store is read-only: commerce changes fail with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED and reason terminal_status. Receipts and order history remain readable.

scheduleFulfillment.description: Sets the start and end of a service fulfillment's appointment window. Read supported_actions for actions available now. occurred_at records when the action occurred; on complete it also records completion evidence. expected_version optionally rejects a stale fulfillment version. Read timeline events with GET /v1/fulfillment-events filtered by package_id, shipment_id, or fulfillment_id, and notifications with GET /v1/fulfillment-notifications filtered by fulfillment_event_id or fulfillment_id.

sendInvoiceReminder.description: Attempts a reminder email for an already issued collectible invoice. Safe to retry with the same idempotency key. Accepts an empty body or {}.

sendMeOrderReceipt.description: Queues a receipt email for one of your paid orders to the order's email. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient.

sendOrderReceipt.description: Queues a receipt for a paid order, including gift card payments and settled payments, and returns the order unchanged. Send email to choose a recipient, or omit it to use the order's email. If no receipt email is on file, email is required when your credential can set it. Otherwise, the request returns ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason configuration_required. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient. Checkout credentials can send only to the address on file. If no address is on file, checkout credentials can send to at most three distinct addresses over the order's lifetime. Receipts sent for this order through this route count toward this limit, including failed deliveries and receipts sent with a secret API key. Merchant callers can choose any address.

sendPaymentIntentReceipt.description: Queues a receipt for a succeeded payment intent and returns the payment intent unchanged. For an order-owned payment intent, sends the order receipt. Once sent, the receipt appears as a receipt_sent payment intent activity. Send email to choose a recipient. Omit email to use the order's receipt address for an order-owned intent, or receipt_email then the customer's email for a standalone intent. If no receipt email is available, email is required. The saved receipt email stays unchanged. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Standalone sending is limited to once every five minutes per payment intent; order receipt sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient. Retry with the same idempotency key to replay the result without sending again.

signWebhookEndpointDelivery.description: Sandbox only. Returns the exact delivery body and headers for an authorized sandbox endpoint without dispatching it. Requires webhooks.write and permission to read the event's resource. JWT signing must be enabled. Each call reauthorizes and creates a fresh five-minute bearer frame; receivers deduplicate webhook-id. Limited to one request per 200 ms and 10,000 per UTC day per endpoint, plus external-provider-action API quotas. The 200 ms throttle returns 429 with Retry-After; daily exhaustion returns 409 LIMIT_REACHED with limit and resets_at and no Retry-After.
